scope: CP1a evidence inputs only; no change to a003 or production geometry, weights, runtime or global shoulder coordinates.

locations: Methods and Table I; Table III; Figures 5-7; Discussion

CL_mm.definition: CL: axis from lateral-end centre to medial-end centre. Surface-end centres are not explicitly identified as articular-surface centres. Curvature fits use 2D projected contour midlines, not 3D centreline arc length.

projected_shape_context.definition: Radii fit circles to superior-view contour midline; conoid position is axial distance of inferior/posterior apex from lateral end divided by CL. Not an articular or rotation centre.

assumptions: All summaries describe the same 350 paired height/CL records partitioned into 102 Japanese and 248 other specimens.
Overall and Japanese CL means printed to one decimal as 143.7 mm; allow a 0.1 mm difference between those unrounded means.
Allow between-group height mean difference as large as the full published 50 cm range.
Allow maximum within-group r=.679 (even .6795 for last-digit rounding leaves upper bound below .692).
conflicts.derivation: Pooled covariance = within covariance + n1*n2/N * delta_x*delta_y. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds within covariance by r_max times total scatter. Therefore pooled r <= r_max + [n1*n2/(N*(N-1))]*abs(delta_x*delta_y)/(s_x*s_y). Inferred between-group CL mean difference <= N/n2*0.1 mm.
conflicts.decision: Reject .968 as a regression input until paired raw data or corrected primary statistic resolves the contradiction. Do not replace it with a guessed correlation.
conflicts.figure_review: Author-institution primary PDF Figures 5/6 visually inspected; both show substantial residual scatter. No points digitized and no regression estimated from the figure. Figure 5 regresses height on CL; do not invert the drawn fit to predict CL from height.

conflicts.decision: Ratios numerically align with R/CL, not CL/R. Treat direction as unresolved wording; never invert them to generate an anatomical curve without endpoint/shape verification.
Record mm context with explicit printed-unit conflict; 34.1 cm cannot fit the reported ~144 mm axial bone. No 10x scaling.

limits: No male-specific height SD/covariance or usable height-to-CL regression supplied. Do not scale male mean by stature ratio.
Do not merge surface-end chord with Qiu articular-centre chord or Bernat 3D arc length.
Two projected fitted radii do not uniquely specify a 3D S-curve, endpoint tangents, twist or SC/AC contacts.
Institution, sex and ethnicity effects do not constitute independent replication; unique subject provenance needed.

languth_review.decision: No bilateral SC breadth extracted; diameter is ventral-to-dorsal bone envelope, not side-to-side joint spacing. No exact coordinates, contact surfaces or orientation targets selected.
limits: Headline sample size is not the usable count for every measurement.
Referenced external values in Table 6 are not new independent cohorts measured by this study.
Large sample size does not repair poor interreader reproducibility.

qiu_SD_correction.corrected_basis: per-bone SD across 52 bilateral clavicles from 26 men; paired observations are not 52 independent people. Between-person dispersion and effective sample size cannot be inferred from this SD alone.
qiu_SD_correction.reason: Earlier claim that bilateral per-bone SD understates between-person SD had no basis; paired dependence concerns inference/effective sample size and does not establish a direction of SD change.

required_next: Independent endpoint-matched articular-centre chord with stature context; primary endpoint diagram/raw geometry for Fontana if used.
SC articular landmarks relative to manubrium and canonical thorax, not surface biacromial breadth or clavicle AP diameter.
Full scapular/AC/GH contact geometry and neutral global pose before global placement.
